answer: A port-authority model resists fake identities: new agents start at a jetty, a small supervised berth where they can only run low-value jobs while their work is checked. Reputation rises slowly, like a tide that only lifts with completed, verified deliveries. A fake fleet trying to launch a voyage of many identities at once faces the same slow onboarding cost per identity, so thousands of sock puppets cost thousands of supervised berths and months of honest work, more than the attack is worth.
